newsitem.title: ITALY: Banca di Roma plans bond issues worth up to $3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Banca di Roma plans bond issues worth up to $3 bln.

text.p: Italy's Banca di Roma said on Tuesday it had organised a medium term note programme for the issue of bonds worth up to $3.0 billion.
"The programme means Banca di Roma will be able to issue on the international markets bonds or other debt instruments to take advantage of the best market conditions," the bank said in a statement.
It said the future issues would have a duration of anything between one month and 30 years, and would be either fixed rate, floating rate or zero coupon.
The bank said the operation was organised by Lehman Brothers with the backing of Barclays de Zoete Wedd, Goldman Sachs, Merrill Lynch, Midland Bank, Nomura and Swiss Bank Co.
Banca di Roma recently launched three issues on the Euro market -- one for $500 million, one for 100 million sterling and one for 250 million marks. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
